recommendations.rationale: The only executed candidate (control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0 -> 0.01) is frozen-classified physical_pareto_worsening against the baseline: candidate holding max speed 1.8234037466740822 vs 1.5810152739742807 m/s, holding max error 0.06344380037515782 vs 0.05813810428573256 m, terminal error 0.008104100271647987 vs 0.007642608585867386 m, mean complete update +0.5668305943121332 s, deadline misses unchanged. Both runs pass reach-only acceptance and fail sampled holding on position and speed. No further candidate or saved-state check is authorized in this phase, so the disposition is defer.

Raising the holding tip-speed weight did not reduce sampled holding tip speed in this paired comparison, which weakens the zero-tip-speed-cost hypothesis but does not refute it (one seed pair, weight 0.01 against tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02, no counterfactual replay). Any further test of this or an alternative lever requires a new explicit control grant, a bounded change and a complete-execution comparison judged by joint reach-plus-holding acceptance with componentwise physical comparison; none of that is executable or authorized here.

The retained evidence supports description only: the holding failure is confined to the sampled final window (continuous_time_guarantee false), 35 wall-clock deadline misses do not establish skipped simulated updates or actuator delay, and full warm plans/iteration traces are not retained with no causal-identification capability available. Attribute no dominant cause from this pair.

attribution.reason: This was the previously 'possible' hypothesis. The authorized bounded candidate raised holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0 -> 0.01 and the pair is classified physical_pareto_worsening: candidate holding max speed is higher (1.8234037466740822 vs 1.5810152739742807 m/s), holding max error is higher (0.06344380037515782 vs 0.05813810428573256 m) and terminal error is marginally higher, with both runs still failing sampled holding and still passing reach. So this parameter change did not improve settling in this paired comparison, and the zero holding tip-speed weight is not shown to be the driver of the sampled holding failure. Weakening, not refutation: one seed pair, one weight magnitude (0.01 against tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02), and no closed-loop counterfactual or retained warm plans, so a small change does not establish equivalence for other magnitudes or other levers.

In both executions the official reach-only criterion is satisfied (reach_passed true, task_bound observed 0.008104100271647985 m inside limit 0.01 m, evaluation task_success true). The recorded failure is confined to the sampled holding window, so terminal reach is not the failed condition in either run.

Both runs report 35 deadline misses at control_period_s 0.01 s with a handed-over mean complete update time near 17.3-17.8 s, and stop-status/status counters are dominated by non-convergence signals (baseline Solve_Succeeded 1 / User_Requested_Stop 34; candidate feasible_early_stop 34 / Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded 1) with only 5-6 non-initialization plans accepted. That pattern remains consistent with plans being chosen under an early-stop/budget policy, but full warm plans and iteration traces are not retained and no counterfactual replay exists, so an effect on holding behaviour is neither shown nor excluded. Wall overruns alone are not evidence of skipped simulated updates.

Selection counts remain initialization-dominated (29 initialization-selected vs 6 non-initialization-selected in the baseline summary; 5 accepted non-initialization plans in the candidate), but neither run retains full warm plans or optimizer iteration traces and no closed-loop counterfactual capability exists, so a link between warm-seed/initialization selection and the sampled holding outcome cannot be established or excluded.

Scheduling is synchronous: controller calls complete before fixed backend steps, and the 35 recorded deadline misses do not inject simulated delay or skip simulated updates. Wall overruns therefore cannot by themselves explain the sampled holding-window position/speed failure.

The one executed control-side change produced physical Pareto worsening across every physical component (terminal error, holding max error, holding max speed), and no retained artifact tests a geometry or discretization alternative. Lack of evidence for a beneficial geometry change does not establish that geometry cannot affect settling or computation; this remains untested, and force proximity alone would not imply a required design change.

facts.statement: The executed candidate improvement-7a36cd1a7c0d (execution 4f5df885e88b40888fe653663129d27e, effective design identity 05ff4f76568044f4a4795290b501107eec4585a5e3e27afe1eece3298f8eae4c) changed only one recipe field relative to the frozen baseline: control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight from baseline 0.0 to effective 0.01; the terminal_tip_speed_weight entry in the design statement carries baseline delta 0.0. Numerical source remains bundled_guess. Coverage: handed-over design statement and execution scope only.

The candidate profile result (artifact 6b50c6f4f69227078175aa2428310ad5056b90f5cbefb47fd46b39b5ac3048b8, source execution 4f5df885e88b40888fe653663129d27e) reports sampled_settling available = true with passed = false, max_error_m = 0.06344380037515782 m and max_speed_m_s = 1.8234037466740822 m/s against position_limit_m = 0.01 m and speed_limit_m_s = 0.02 m/s, while the recorded task bound was satisfied with observed 0.008104100271647985 m against limit 0.01 m (terminal_error_m 0.008104100271647987 m). The same result records 5 accepted non-initialization plans. Coverage: run-level profile scalars and recorded evaluation entries; not per-sample rows.

Baseline execution cf997605885642759ee33920e2c9e2ef: reach_passed = true with terminal_error_m = 0.007642608585867386 m; the recorded final holding window (six samples 0.30-0.35 s) shows error_m range 0.007642608585867386 to 0.05813810428573256 m and speed_m_s range 0.6351726092425104 to 1.5810152739742807 m/s, with holding_speed_passed = false. So in the baseline the terminal endpoint is inside the position limit while the sampled holding window is not. Coverage: run-level summary scalars plus final-window aggregates; not whole-trajectory rows.

The frozen campaign comparison of candidate minus baseline (program-derived from the sealed evaluations/profiles) classifies the pair as physical_pareto_worsening, with deltas holding_max_error_m +0.0053056960894252575 m, holding_max_speed_m_s +0.24238847269980157 m/s, terminal_error_m +0.00046149168578060035 m, mean_complete_update_s +0.5668305943121332 s and deadline_misses +0; both sides report official reach task success true, valid complete executions, real-time not demonstrated, and sampled holding speed not passed. There is no physical component that improved. Coverage: two complete sealed executions at control_period_s 0.01 s.

Official reach-only acceptance is satisfied for both executions (evaluation task_success = true; task_bound observed 0.008104100271647985 m against limit 0.01 m; valid_complete_execution = true), and this is distinct from joint reach-plus-holding success, which is recorded false for both because the sampled final-window position and speed criteria are not met. Terminal reach pass therefore does not imply settling success in either run. Coverage: run-level verdicts, not continuous-time verification.

Completion and computation: the candidate simulation receipt status is completed with simulation charge 627.438000000082 s and 35 control updates at control_period_s 0.01 s, total_updates 35, force_bound_violation_n 0.0 and solver_error_count 0; 35 deadline misses are reported for both runs. Baseline stopping counts are Solve_Succeeded 1 / User_Requested_Stop 34 at the displayed summary level, and the candidate optimization status counts are feasible_early_stop 34 / Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded 1. These are wall-clock and status observations; synchronous wall overruns do not establish skipped simulated updates. Coverage: run-level counters plus selected per-update rows.

Structured holding feedback for the candidate records frame world, coverage_complete = true over interval 0.30-0.35 s with 6 samples, position_limit_m 0.01 m, and continuous_time_guarantee = false. The holding verdict is therefore a sampled statement over the final six samples, not a continuous-time guarantee and not a whole-trajectory range. Coverage: final 0.05 s window only.

No retained artifact supports closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal identification (capabilities list 'causal_identification' as unsupported; inventory capability gap 'No closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution tool'), and full warm plans / optimizer iteration traces are not retained (control_snapshots.json absent; limitation 'No historical optimizer iterations or full warm plans are reconstructed'). Consequently the observed Pareto worsening and the residual holding-window speed (0.64-1.82 m/s against a 0.02 m/s limit) cannot be assigned to a mechanism from retained evidence. Coverage: availability statements about retained evidence only.

limitations: This revision phase had zero evidence turns and authorizes no further candidate or saved-state check; all numbers above come from retained/transferred content (baseline common summary, the handed-over complete improvement feedback for candidate improvement-7a36cd1a7c0d, and the frozen campaign comparison).

Both the terminal reach and the sampled holding verdicts are run-level or final-window-level: reach is evaluated at the last execution sample and holding over the six retained samples 0.30-0.35 s, with continuous_time_guarantee false. No continuous-time claim and no whole-trajectory range is made.

Some handed-over fields have no handle in this context's displayed fact catalogue (e.g. candidate converged_updates, mean_complete_update_s, deadline_misses, per_update_delivery_s rows, and the campaign candidate_minus_baseline deltas); they are reported from the handed-over content and are not certified by the selected handles.

Selected rows only: motion view coverage is the final 0.05 s window; per-update computation rows in the catalogue are a subset of the 35 updates. The sampled update at which holding speed stops decreasing and the first sampled update inside tolerance are not located from displayed rows.

Single seed per side (seed 17) and a single changed field at one magnitude: a comparison of one weight change does not establish equivalence of configurations, and derived arithmetic from sealed evaluations does not certify the prose interpretation.

Full historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces (control_snapshots.json) are not retained, and no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution capability exists; the observed Pareto worsening and the residual holding speed therefore have no retained mechanistic attribution.
recommended_actions: Retain the deferral on control changes: the only executed candidate (holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0 -> 0.01) is classified physical_pareto_worsening against the frozen baseline (higher holding max speed 1.8234037466740822 vs 1.5810152739742807 m/s, higher holding max error 0.06344380037515782 vs 0.05813810428573256 m, marginally higher terminal error, no deadline-miss change), with both runs passing reach and failing sampled holding; no execution, parameter change or saved-state check is authorized in this phase.

If further work is granted, treat the tip-speed-weight lever as weakened rather than resolved: a new explicit control grant would be needed for a different magnitude or a different lever (e.g. holding_brake_lead_s, horizon, terminal_weight), and it must be judged by joint reach-plus-holding acceptance plus componentwise physical comparison, not by computation alone.

Do not attribute the sampled holding failure to wall-clock deadline misses, to skipped simulated updates, or to terminal reach: reach passed, scheduling is synchronous, and 35 deadline misses are a wall-clock observation only.

Before any further control decision, acquire the per-update computation table (deadline_missed, unusable_updates, update_wall_s, optimization_status/raw_status, selected iteration, effective horizon for all 35 updates of both runs) and the per-sample trajectory rows over 0.01-0.35 s; both are retained inventory entries but were only partially displayed here.
